title: PrP-targeting siRNA Safety & Mechanism Study
official: An Open-label, Single Ascending Dose Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Intrathecally Administered PrP-siRNA in Adults Diagnosed With Symptomatic Prion Disease and in Pre-symptomatic Adults at Genetic Risk for Prion Disease.
summary: The purpose of this trial is to evaluate safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamic impact of PrP-siRNA in symptomatic prion disease patients and in pre-symptomatic adults at genetic risk for prion disease.
criteria:
Key inclusion criteria for symptomatic patients:

1. clinically manifested symptoms of prion disease, in the opinion of the investigator
2. a diagnosis of probable prion disease according to CDC criteria
3. a positive CSF RT-QuIC or PRNP genetic test
4. no more than moderate functional impairment as quantified by an MRC-PDRS score ≥15
5. availability of a caregiver to assist with study procedures

Key inclusion criteria for pre-symptomatic patients:

1. lack of clinically manifested symptoms of prion disease, as demonstrated by an MRC Score of 20, a MoCA score between 24-30 inclusive, and a neurological exam with no clinically significant findings, in the opinion of the investigator
2. a PRNP genetic test indicating the presence of a highly penetrant genetic variant causal for prion disease

Key exclusion criteria for all arms:

1. pregnancy or unwillingness to comply with the contraceptive requirements during the study period
2. contraindication to lumbar puncture
3. recent participation in a different prion disease clinical trial

Additional inclusion and exclusion criteria apply and will be evaluated at screening.
